title: After a restart anti-rug re-registers each position with the first dex of its pool type, not the dex it was bought on, so a position on a chain second V2 dex (every chain has two) gets its emergency exit routed through the wrong router

evidence.note: ctx.chain.dexes.find(d => d.dexType === trade.pool_type): first dex of that type
dex_name is recorded on the buy row (bot.ts:1145, :1469 pass dex.name), so the right dex is known and not used
the dex is stored on the RegisteredPosition
it is passed to triggerAntiRugExit, which calls executeFullSell(ctx, dex, ...) (exitTrigger.ts:266)
the V3 sell simulation uses position.dex.quoterAddress
ETH lists uniswap-v2 and sushiswap-v2; BSC lists two V2 and two V3 (:238-264), Base two V2 (:302-321), Arbitrum two V2 (:359-378)

sibling_sites_checked: AUD-EXIT-013 records the same first-of-type choice for the exit-monitor resume (bot.ts:1940-1956) and the dashboard sells (controls.ts findDex); its sibling list does not name this anti-rug resume site (bot.ts:2098), which is why this is a separate entry. The registrations at buy time (bot.ts:440, :1492) pass the correct dex. The backfill and dispatch paths use whatever dex the registration stored.
severity_rationale: S1, as AUD-EXIT-013. After any restart, every position bought on a second dex has an anti-rug exit that sells through a router whose factory either has no pair for the token (the sell reverts) or a different pool. On BSC V3 the sell simulation hits the other dex quoter, reverts, and trips signal 3 (fail-closed), so the trigger fires and the escape fails. Restarts are routine, and half of the V2 dexes are second dexes. Merged at 22-28 into AUD-EXIT-013 (canonical): same defect, one root cause (the resume path picks the first dex of the pool type instead of the stored dex_name), one fix, card EXIT-10.
recommendation: Resolve the dex from trades.dex_name on resume, for both the exit monitor and anti-rug (card EXIT-10). Phase 24.
